questions.question: Who was the first female Muslim ruler of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__ Razia Sultana.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Razia Sultana was the first female Muslim ruler of the Indian subcontinent.
 
• She ruled in Delhi from 1236 to 1240 as the Sultan herself – it was a title never before bestowed on a woman, a position of power never before attained by a woman.
 
• Before ascending to the throne of Delhi after her father’s death, the reign was briefly handed over to her half-brother Rukn ud-din Firuz.
 
• But after Firuz’s assassination within 6 months of his ascendency, the nobles agreed to place Razia on the throne.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__Slave Dynasty __

 
• Established by Qutb ud-Din Aibak.
 
• Dynasty lasted from 1206 to 1290.
 
• It was the first of the dynasties to rule as the Delhi Sultanate.
 
• Dynasty ended when Jalal ud din Firuz Khilji overthrew the last Mamluk ruler Muiz ud din Qaiqabad in 1290.
 
• Dynasty was succeeded by the Khilji (or Khalji) dynasty, the second dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate.

questions.question: Who among the following rulers was a part of the Tripartite Struggle for the possession of Kannauj?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dharmapala**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dharmapala** was one of the significant rulers involved in the Tripartite Struggle for the possession of Kannauj.
 
• The Tripartite Struggle was a prolonged conflict among three powerful dynasties: the **Gurjara-Pratiharas**, the **Palas**, and the **Rashtrakutas**.
 
• Dharmapala was the ruler of the **Pala Dynasty** and played a crucial role in the contest for Kannauj, a region of strategic importance in Northern India.
 
• During his reign, Dharmapala extended his influence over Northern India and sought to establish his supremacy over Kannauj.
 
• The struggle for Kannauj had significant implications for the control of trade routes and political dominance in the region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Tripartite Struggle** lasted for nearly two centuries and was characterized by shifting alliances and frequent battles.
 
• The city of **Kannauj** was highly coveted due to its prime location and economic significance.
 
• Other notable rulers involved in the Tripartite Struggle include **Rashtrakuta King Dhruva** and **Gurjara-Pratihara King Nagabhata II**.
 
• The struggle eventually weakened all three dynasties, paving the way for the rise of new powers in the Indian subcontinent.

questions.question: The founder of the Pala empire was:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gopala**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gopala** was the founder of the Pala Empire.
 
• The Pala Empire was an imperial power during the Late Classical period on the Indian subcontinent, which originated in the region of Bengal.
 
• Gopala was elected as the ruler by a group of regional chieftains and gained control over the areas of Bihar and Bengal.
 
• He laid the foundation of the Pala dynasty which ruled from the 8th to the 12th century.
 
• The Pala Empire is known for its patronage of Buddhism and the establishment of many Buddhist institutions and structures.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Palas were known for their contribution to the cultural and educational development of the region.
 
• The famous universities of Nalanda and Vikramashila flourished under their rule.
 
• The Pala Empire was succeeded by the Sena dynasty in the 12th century.
 
• The founder of the Pala dynasty, Gopala, was succeeded by his son Dharmapala, who expanded the empire significantly.
 
• The Pala rulers also had diplomatic relations with other Asian countries, including the Tibetan Empire.

questions.question: Name the Chola inscription that provided details of the way in which the sabha was organised in the local administration in the Chola empire.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** the Uttaramerur inscription**** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• ** **The **Uttaramerur Inscription** is the Chola inscription that provides detailed information about the organization of the **sabha** (village assembly) in the local administration during the Chola Empire
 
• It **outlines the criteria for becoming a member of the assembly**, the qualifications required for candidates, the process of electing members,
 
 
• and the responsibilities of different committees.
 
 
 
• The** inscription is found in Uttaramerur**, a village in present-day Tamil Nadu.
 
• The inscription mentions the system of **kudavolai** (lottery) for electing members to the various committees of the sabha
 
• The Uttaramerur inscription showcases the **highly decentralized administrative structure of the Chola Empire**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Darsanam Koppu Inscription**

 
 
• **It ​**refers to an inscription found during the reign of the Cholas.
 
• It is notable for its reference to land grants or donations made to temples or religious institutions.
 
• This type of inscription typically provides insights into the administrative setup during the Chola period
 
• It highlights the practice of **temple endowments** (land grants given to temples), 4
 
 
• showing the interrelationship between rulers and religious bodies in medieval India.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Thiruvalangadu Inscription**
 
 
• **​**The **Thiruvalangadu inscription** is one of the most famous Chola inscriptions, commissioned by **Rajaraja Chola I**,
 
 
• who ruled in the 11th century. It is located in the **Thiruvalangadu** temple, near Kanchipuram in Tamil Nadu.
 
 
 
• This inscription provides a detailed eulogy of the Chola king Rajaraja I, tracing the lineage of the Chola dynasty and celebrating his military achievements.
 
• It includes references to his conquests in South India, Sri Lanka, and the Maldives.
 
 
 
• **Thirunanthikarai Inscription****​**
 
 
• The Thirunanthikarai inscription shows the influence of the Ay dynasty in the region,
 
 
• providing evidence of land ownership, local governance, and religious endowments.
 
 
 
• It also highlights the cultural and economic exchanges between the different South Indian kingdoms during this period
 
• The inscription, written in **Vattezhuthu script**, records a land grant made during the reign of the **Ay kings**. 
 
 

ba:T

questions.question: Who amongst the following Delhi Sultanate rulers sent his army under Malik Kafur’s command to conquer South India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Alauddin Khilji**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Alauddin Khilji** was a prominent ruler of the Delhi Sultanate who reigned from 1296 to 1316.
 
• He is known for his military conquests and administrative reforms.
 
• Alauddin Khilji sent his trusted general, **Malik Kafur**, to lead expeditions to South India.
 
• Under Malik Kafur's command, the army successfully raided several kingdoms in the Deccan and South India, including the Yadavas, Kakatiyas, and Hoysalas.
 
• These expeditions were significant as they brought immense wealth to the Delhi Sultanate and expanded its influence to the southern regions of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ghiyas-ud-din Balban** was a ruler of the Delhi Sultanate who focused more on consolidating power in the north rather than expanding southward.
 
• **Qutub-al-din Aibak** was the founder of the Delhi Sultanate and laid the foundation for future rulers but did not engage in significant southern expeditions.
 
• **Iltutmish** was another significant ruler who consolidated the Sultanate's power in the north and built the administrative framework but did not send expeditions to South India.
 
• The Delhi Sultanate was a series of dynasties that ruled northern India from the 13th to the 16th centuries, with significant contributions to Indian culture, architecture, and administration.

questions.question: The founders of the Vijayanagara Empire were the feudatories of which of the following dynasties?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kakatiya**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The founders of the Vijayanagara Empire** were the **feudatories Kakatiya dynasty**.
 
• Before establishing the Vijayanagara Empire in **1336, Harihara and Bukka**, who were initially feudatories of the Kakatiyas of Warangal, served in administrative roles for both the Kakatiya and Kampili kingdoms.
 
• Following the Muslim conquest of Kakatiya in 1323, they sought refuge in Kampili, where they eventually rose to become ministers.
 
• The Vijayanagara Empire, founded by Harihara and Bukka, emerged after their time in Kampili.
 
• Over its history, the empire saw the rule of significant dynasties including the** Sangama, Saluva, Tuluva, and Aravidu**. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Hoysala Empire**, a significant Kannadiga power in the Indian subcontinent, held sway over much of present-day Karnataka from the 10th to the 14th centuries. Initially headquartered in Belur, the capital later shifted to Halebidu.
 
• **The Pandyan dynasty,** also known as the Pandyas of Madurai, stood as an ancient Tamil dynasty in South India, counted among the prominent kingdoms of Tamilakam alongside the Pallavas, the Cholas, and the Cheras.
 
• Originating from southern India, the **Chola dynasty** governed the expansive Chola Empire, a prominent maritime power. The earliest verifiable mentions of the Chola date back to inscriptions dating to the 3rd century BCE during the Maurya empire under Ashoka's reign.

questions.question: Who among the following did Babur defeat in the year 1528 at Chanderi?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Medni Rai__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Battle of Chanderi** took place in the aftermath of the **Battle of Khanwa** in which the Mughal Emperor **Babur had defeated the Rajput Confederacy** and firmly established **Mughal rule.**
 
• **Babur** decided to **isolate the Rana** by inflicting a military defeat on one of his vassals **Medini Rai** who was the **ruler of Malwa.**
 
• Consequently, in December 1527, taking a circumlocutious route **Babur marched to the fortress of Chanderi** in **Malwa **which was the capital of the kingdom of **Malwa**.
 
• Upon reaching Chanderi, on** 20 January 1528**, Babur offered Shamsabad to **Medini Rai in exchange for Chanderi** as a peace overture but **the offer was rejected by Rai.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The first battle of Panipat - 21 April 1526
 
• The second battle of Panipat - 5 November 1556
 
• The third battle of Panipat - 14 January 1761
 
• Battle of Khanwa - March 16, 1527.
 
• Battle of Halighati - 18 June 1576
 
• Battle of Buxar - 22/23 October 1764

questions.question: Shaikh Muinuddin Sijzi (Moinuddin Chishti) dargah is situated in which of the following cities.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ajmer**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ajmer Sharif Dargah/ Ajmer Dargah/Ajmer Sharif/Dargah Sharif is a Sufi tomb of the revered Sufi saint; Moinuddin Chishti.**
 
• It is located at** Ajmer** comprised of Chishti's grave.
 
• **Chishti** was a **charismatic and compassionate spiritual preacher and teacher.**
 
• The biographical accounts of his life written after his death report that he received the gifts of many "spiritual marvels (karāmāt), such as miraculous travel, clairvoyance, and visions of angels" in these years of his life.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**Other important sufi saints:**

 
• Khwaja Moinuddin Chisti

 
 
• Khwaja Moinuddin Chisti also popularly known as Khwaja Gareeb Nawaz was a beloved Sufi saint of the Chisti order.
 
• He is known to be the direct descendant of Prophet Muhammad.
 
• Born in Sistan (present-day Eastern Iran and Southern Afghanistan, he travelled from Sistan to Lahore to Delhi, and finally settled in Ajmer, Rajasthan.
 
• His tomb in Ajmer, the Ajmer Sharif Dargah, is one of the holiest Islamic sites in the world.
 
• Muslims from across the world visit Dargah Sharif every year to offer their prayers.
 
• Not only Muslims but people belonging to different religions visit this shrine throughout the year.
 
 
 
• Baba Farid
 
 
• Baba Sheikh Farid as he is called all over Punjab, India, and Pakistan was born at the time when Punjab was going through great crossroads.
 
• Timur the Lame, Halaku (Son of Changez Khan), etc ravaged Punjab about 100 to 200 years before he was born.
 
• The Slave dynasty of Qutub-Ud-Din aibak was at that time being ruled by Sultan Balban. 200-300 years earlier to the West of India, the sword of Islam had swept in the countries like Iran, Afghanistan, and Eastern Europe.
 
• In India too, Slave Qutubdin Aibak tried to subdue people through force, but could only create a rift between different communities.
 
• Then came the Sufi saints from Arabia and other places to spread their message of love for Allah.
 
• Sufi saints like Khwaja Qutub-Ul-Din Bakhtiar Kaki, who was a Sayid of the Jafiri Hussaini tribe, were very famous.
 
 
 
• Qutubuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki
 
 
• Hazrat Khawaja Bakhtiyar Kaaki‎ was one and a half years old when his father passed away.
 
• Khawaja Qutubuddeen Bakhtiyar Kaaki‎ learned 15 chapters of the Holy Quran from his mother and his mother arranged for his further education and training.

questions.question: In 711 CE, Arab general _______ conquered Sind, which became a part of the Caliph’s domain.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **711 CE, Arab General Muhammad Qasim** conquered the Sind province.
 
• It was the **first Arab victory in India** and it led to the foundation for **Arab invasion in India.**
 
• He succeeded in conquering Sind in his third attempt in which he defeated Dahir, the King of Sind.
 
• **Muhammad Bin Qasim**__
 __
 
• He is also known as** Laquab of Imad-ad-Din.**
 
• He was born on **31st December, 695 AD.**
 
• He was the **first Muslim to invade** India and was the** commander of the Umayyad Caliphate.**
 
• He was sent as a prisoner to Mesopotamia.
 
• In 711 AD he defeated Raja Dahir.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Muhammad Ghori**__

 __
 
• He was the third Muslim ruler who invaded India.
 
• His real name was Shahabuddin allas Muizudin Muhammad Ghori.
 
• He was defeated by Prithviraj in the First Battle of Tarain in 1191 AD and recovered Bhatinda.
 
• In the second battle of Tarain (1192AD) the joined forces of the Rajput rulers under Prithviraj were defeated by Muhammad Ghori. Prithviraj was held as a prisoner and later put to death.
 
• **Qutb-Ud-din Aibak** was appointed as the **commander by Muhammad of Ghori.**
 
 
 
• **Qutub-ud-din Aibak**__
 __
 
• ​He was the **first Sultan of Delhi in 1206 AD.**
 
• He was in charge of the **Ghurid territories and later became the ruler of the Delhi Sultanate** ruled by the **Mamluk Dynasty 1,1210.**
 
• He is known for commissioning the **Qutub Minar in Delhi.****​**
 
 
 
• **Muhammad-Bin-Tughlaq**__
 
 
• ​He was the **Sultan of Delhi from 1325 to 1351.**
 
• He was the **eldest son of Ghiyas-ud-din Tughlaq** the** founder of the Tughlaq dynasty.**
 
• In 1327, he** shifted his capital from Delhi to Daulatbad** in the **Deccan, in present-day Maharashtra**.

questions.question: When was the Treaty of Purandar signed between Shivaji and Jai Singh I?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **1665**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Treaty of Purandar, 1665 was signed between the Jai Singh I and Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj.
 
• This treaty was signed on 11th June 1665.
 
• Raja Jai Singh was signed on behalf of the Mughal Emperor Aurangzeb.
 
• Shivaji agreed to surrender 23 forts to the Emperor while the Emperor recognized Shivaji’s authority over 12 forts including Rajgarh and its revenue.
 
• Shivaji promised to supply for imperial service 5000 soldiers under his son Shambhaji and the Emperor agreed to assign a suitable jagir for their maintenance.
 
• Shivaji declined to accept any mansab but promised to fight on behalf of the emperor whenever demanded.
 
• There were some secret clauses in the treaty as well, which provided for Shivaji’s participation in the war against Bijapur on behalf of the Emperor.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information:__**

 
• Jai Singh, I became the King of Amber and Head of the Kachwaha Rajput at the age of 10.
 
• Raja Jai Singh is the descendant of Raja Man Singh, and he is one of the famous nav-ratnas of Emperor Akbar. 
 
• The fort of Amer (or Amber) near Jaipur, Rajasthan is used to be their capital.
 
• Shivaji is the founder of the Maratha Kingdom in India.
 
• In 1674, he was formally crowned as the Chhatrapati (Monarch) of his realm at Raigad.
 
• Shivaji established a competent and progressive civil rule with the help of a disciplined military and well-structured administrative organisations.

questions.question: Alha and Udal, who gave stiff resistance to the enemy, belonged to which of the following Rajput States?
questions.solution: The correct answer is __**Chandella**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** • **Alha **and **Udal** were legendary generals in the **service of King Parmardi-deva **(also known as **Parmal**), who belonged to the **Chandela dynasty.** • Their bravery and resistance against enemies are celebrated in the **epic ballad Alha-Khand**. • They were** born to Chandravanshiya Kshatriya family**. Udal was 12 years younger than Alha. • They learned the art of war and religious knowledge from **their guru, Gorakhnath**. • Alha and Udal were the learned scholars who shared a long-lasting bond between them. questions.question: Who among the following appointed Aziz Khummar a wine distiller to high administrative post?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Muhammad Tughluq.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Muhammad Tughluq appointed Ladha and Pira, two gardeners to high administrative posts.
 
• Sultan Muhammad Tughluq appointed:
 
 
• Aziz Khummar, a wine distiller,
 
• Firuz Hajjam, a barber,
 
• Manka Tabbakh, a cook, and
 
• Two gardeners, Ladha and Pira, to high administrative posts.
 
 
 
• Ziyauddin Barani, a mid-fourteenth-century chronicler, reported their appointments as a sign of Sultan’s loss of political judgment and his incapacity to rule.
 
• Barani had criticized Muhammad Tughluq for that appointment.
 
• Tughluq's appointment reflected the socio-economic stereotypes that may have been prevalent in those times.
 
• The authors of Persian tawarikh criticized the Delhi Sultans for appointing the “low and base-born” to high offices.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Allauddin Khalji

 
 
• ​Allauddin Khalji was the emperor of the Khalji dynasty.
 
• He was known to drive back the Mongols' invasion from India.
 
• Alauddin instituted a number of significant administrative changes, related to revenues, price controls, and society. 
 
• Alauddin conquered the kingdoms of Gujarat, Jaisalmer, Ranthambore, Chittor, Malwa, Siwana and Jalore. 
 
 
 
• **Jalaluddin Khalji**

 
• The founder of the Khilji dynasty was Jalal-Ud-din Firuz Khalji.
 
• He was also called “Clemency Jalal-uddin” as he followed peace and wanted to rule without violence.
 
• He appointed Ala-ud-din Khilji as the Governor of Kara. Alauddin was his son-in-law and also nephew.
 
• Jalal-ud-din was treacherously murdered by Ala-Ud-din Khilji his son-in-law.

 
• Firuz Shah Tughluq

 
• He was the third ruler of the Tughlaq dynasty after the death of Mohammad-bin Tughlaq.
 
• He imposed Jizya tax on all non-Muslims and did not even exempt Brahmins and beggers as done by his predecessors.
 
• He built Feroz Shah Kotla (Kotla means fortress), peppered Delhi with gardens, constructed canals, hunting lodges, and repaired Qutub Minar, Hauz Khas (royal tank), and Surajkund (lake of the Sun).

questions.question: Who defeated Mohammad Ghori in the First Battle of Tarain fought in the year 1191?

__
 
• **First Battle of Tarain (1191):**

 
 
• Participants: Prithviraj Chauhan vs. Muhammad of Ghori.
 
• Outcome:** Victory for Prithviraj Chauhan.**
 
 
 
• **Second Battle of Tarain (1192):**
 
 
• Participants: Prithviraj Chauhan vs. Muhammad of Ghori.
 
• Outcome: **Decisive victory for Muhammad of Ghori.**
 
• Consequence: Prithviraj Chauhan was captured and executed; **established Muslim rule in northern India.**
 
• Significance:
 
 
• **Paved the way for the Delhi Sultanate.**
 
• **Qutb-ud-din Aibak, Muhammad of Ghori's former slave, **founded the Mamluk Dynasty in 1206, establishing the first Delhi Sultanate.
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Overthrew** the **last Shunga kin**g around 75 BCE.
 
• Ruled parts of northern and central India.
 
• **Yashovarman of Kannauj**: 8th-century king, **founded Varman dynasty**, military conquests, patron of arts, defeated Bengal ruler.
 
• **Vidyadhar: **11th-century ruler of **Chandela dynasty**, fortified Khajuraho temples, resisted Ghaznavid invasions, patron of architecture.

questions.question: The Palas were:

options.text: a dynasty that first appeared in Cambodia

• Period: Ruled from the 8th to 12th centuries.
 
• Founder: Gopala established the dynasty around the 8th century.
 
• Regions: Primarily Bengal and parts of Bihar.
 
 
 
• **Religious and Cultural Contributions:**
 
 
• Buddhism: The Palas were prominent patrons of Mahayana Buddhism.
 
• Educational Institutions: Founded and supported renowned Buddhist universities like Nalanda and Vikramashila.
 
 
 
• **Key Rulers:**
 
 
• Dharma Pala (circa 770–810 CE): Consolidated and expanded the empire, strengthening its influence.
 
• Devapala (circa 810–850 CE): Furthered the empire's reach and prosperity.
 
 
 
• **Decline and Legacy:**
 
 
• The empire declined due to invasions by the Cholas and the rise of new regional powers, including the Senas.
 
• The Palas are remembered for their significant contributions to art, architecture, and the promotion of Buddhist learning and culture in the Indian subcontinent.

questions.question: Which amongst the following Sultans shifted his capital from Delhi to Daulatabad?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Muhammad Bin Tughlaq**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Muhammad Bin Tughlaq** was the Sultan who shifted his capital from Delhi to Daulatabad.
 
• This decision was made during his reign in the early 14th century.
 
• The move was intended to help control the Deccan region more effectively and to protect the capital from Mongol invasions.
 
• However, the decision proved to be a failure due to logistical issues and the hardships it caused to the people.
 
• Eventually, the capital was moved back to Delhi.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Muhammad Bin Tughlaq** ruled from 1325 to 1351 and is known for his ambitious but often impractical projects.
 
• He was the second ruler of the Tughlaq dynasty.
 
• His reign is marked by several bold experiments in governance, including the introduction of token currency and tax reforms.
 
• Despite his intelligence and vision, many of his policies were considered ahead of their time and failed due to poor execution.
 
• His decision to shift the capital is often cited as a classic example of his ambitious but flawed administrative decisions.

questions.question: The Battle of Karnal is known for the invasion of which of the following aggressors against India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nadir Shah**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Battle of Karnal** occurred in **1739**, when **Nadir Shah**, the ruler of the Afsharid dynasty of Persia, invaded India.
 
• He** defeated the Mughal army** **led **by **Muhammad Shah** at Karnal and subsequently sacked Delhi, the Mughal capital.
 
• This decisive victory marked the beginning of the decline of the Mughal Empire.
 
• **Afsharid Dynasty**:
 
 
• The **Turkoman Afshar tribe** in **Iran's northeastern area of Khorasan** gave rise to the Afsharid dynasty, which **controlled Iran (Persia) in the middle of the eighteenth century**.
 
• **Nadir Shah (Nader Shah Afshar)**, a brilliant military tactician who deposed the final Safavid dynasty member and crowned himself Shah of Iran, **founded **the **dynasty **in **1736**.
 
• Under Nader's leadership, Iran reached its widest point since the Sasanian Empire.
 
• At its height, it **controlled **portions of **Iraq**, **Turkey**, the **United Arab Emirates**, and **Oman **in addition to modern-day **Iran**, **Armenia**, **Georgia**, the **Azerbaijan **Republic, **Afghanistan**, **Bahrain**, **Turkmenistan**, **Uzbekistan**, and **Pakistan**, as well as portions of the **North Caucasus (Dagestan)**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ahmed Shah Abdali**:

 
 
• The **founder of the Durrani Empire** and the modern state of Afghanistan was Ahmad Shah Abdali, sometimes referred to as Ahmad Khan Abdali or **Ahmad Shah Durrani**.
 
• **After Nadir Shah passed away in 1747**, **Abdali **was selected to** take over **and attacked India on several occasions between 1748 and 1767.
 
• During this period, he **launched eight invasions of India**, conquered Punjab, and **defeated the Marathas** in the **Third Battle of Panipat in 1761**.
 
 
 
• **Shah Shuja**:
 
 
• The **second child** of Mughal Emperor **Shah Jahan** and Empress **Mumtaz Mahal **was Mirza Shah Shuja.
 
• He served as **governor** of both **Bengal **and **Odisha**; his **capital **was **Dhaka**.
 
• Following Shah Jahan's sickness in September of 1657, the brothers had a power struggle.
 
• **Shah Shuja** declared himself to be the Emperor, but **Aurangzeb **took the Dehli throne and dispatched Mir Jumla to bring Shuja under control.
 
• On January 5, **1659**, **Shuja lost** the** Battle of Khajwa**.
 
 
 
• **Nasir Khan**:
 
 
• While Nasir Khan **participated in rebellions against the Mughal Empire**, he wasn't involved in the Battle of Karnal.

questions.question: In which year was the Second Anglo-Mysore war fought between the Kingdom of Mysore and the British East India Company?
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is __**1780-1784.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The second Anglo-Mysore war was fought in **1780-84** between the** Kingdom of Mysore and the British East India Company.**
 
• The immediate cause of the war was the attack on the French port Mahe by British troops led by **Warren Hastings.**
 
• During the war, Hyder Ali died but his son Tipu Sultan continued the struggle.
 
• Meanwhile, the French came to his assistance, and finally, the Treaty of Mangalore (1784) was signed.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The** **First Anglo-Mysore War** - 1767–69
 
• **The Second Anglo-Mysore War**- 1780–84
 
• **The Third Anglo-Mysore War**- 1790–92.
 
• **The Fourth Anglo-Mysore War**- 1798–99.

questions.question: During the rule of Tipu Sultan, which was the capital city of his state Mysore?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Srirangapatnam__**.

__
 
• **Tipu Sultan built this palace in 1784 and ruled Mysore from Srirangapatnam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__****Tipu Sultan** was the ruler of Mysore.

 
• Tipu Sultan is well known as the **“Tiger of Mysore”.**
 
• He had the image of a **tiger on his flag.**
 
• He is the son of the **powerful Mysore** ruler **Haidar Ali.**
 
• **Tipu Sultan** ruled Mysore from **1782 to 1799.**
 
• He maintained a positive relationship with the French in India and modernized his army with their help.
 
• The French commander-in-chief **Napoleon Bonaparte** sought an alliance with Tipu Sultan
 
• The **Treaty of Srirangapatnam (1792)** is associated with Tipu Sultan.
 
• He was killed while defending his capital Seringapatam.
